recover.busy: Recovering the account. This takes a few seconds.
recover.code_help: Ask the administrator of the server for it. It works once and for 24 hours; a newer code replaces it.
recover.done_backup: The server was asked to make a new backup. It is usually made within a few minutes.
recover.done_devices: Every other device and browser was signed out. They sign in again with the new master password.
recover.done_not_signed_in: The account was recovered, but the sign-in afterwards did not go through. Sign in with your new master password.
recover.done_old_files: Exports and backups made before the recovery still open with the old master password and the old recovery key.
recover.done_old_key: Your old recovery key no longer works on this server. If the server is restored from a backup made before today, the old master password and the old recovery key work again and the new ones do not. Keep your old page 2 until you know a new backup has been made.
recover.done_passkeys: Passkeys that were added before the recovery still open the vault. Look at the list and remove any you do not recognise.
recover.done_passkeys_later: If you use passkeys, look at the list under Account › Unlock methods once you are signed in: a recovery leaves the passkeys that were added before it.
recover.done_sheet: Page 1 of your emergency sheet did not change: the QR text and the secret key stay the same.
recover.done_signed_in: You are signed in with your new master password.
recover.error.cancelled: The recovery was stopped before anything was sent. Nothing was changed: the recovery key that was shown is not valid, and your old one still works.
recover.error.code_refused: The code was not accepted. It may be mistyped, used, replaced by a newer code or older than 24 hours, or the e-mail address may be wrong. If you are sure both are right, wait five minutes and try again. Nothing was changed.
recover.error.code_required: Enter the one-time code from the administrator of the server.
recover.error.decrypt: That recovery key does not open this account. Check it against page 2 of your newest emergency sheet. Nothing was changed.
recover.error.denied: The server refused the recovery. Nothing was changed. Start again; if it keeps happening, ask for a new one-time code.
recover.error.not_confirmed: The new recovery key was not typed back, so nothing was sent. Nothing was changed.
recover.error.qr_required: This browser does not know the account yet, so it needs page 1 of your emergency sheet as well: paste the text under the QR code. Nothing was sent.
recover.error.recover_unconfirmed: The recovery may have gone through: the server's answer did not arrive in a form this page can trust. Do not repeat it. Sign in with the new master password first; if that is refused, nothing was changed and your old recovery key still works.
recover.error.rk_required: Enter the recovery key from page 2 of your emergency sheet.
recover.error.unauthorized: The recovery session has ended: it lasts 30 minutes and ends when the account is signed in elsewhere. Nothing was changed. Ask for a new one-time code.
recover.heading: Forgot your master password?
recover.intro: Recover the account with your recovery key and choose a new master password. You are never asked for the old one. Every other device and browser is signed out.
recover.new_browser: On a browser that has not been used with this account you need both pages of your emergency sheet: the QR text and the secret key from page 1, and the recovery key from page 2. A device that remembers the account needs only page 2, and the secret key if it does not remember that.
recover.offer.old_sheet: The server says it was restored from a backup made before you last changed your master password and renewed your recovery key. If you restored the server yourself: your newest recovery key does not work on this server. The recovery key on the sheet you had before the renewal does, but this device never goes back to an older key. Choose "Forget this server on this device", then recover with that older sheet, or sign in with the master password the server knows. If you did not restore the server yourself, this can be an attack: do not forget the server, and contact the person who runs it.
recover.offer.recover: The server says it was restored from a backup made before you last changed your master password. This device refuses the older password to protect you. If you restored the server yourself, use your recovery key: recover the account and type your newest master password as the new one. If you did not, this can be an attack: contact the person who runs the server.
recover.password_help: At least 12 characters with a secret key, 15 without. Use it from now on; the recovery key is the only way back if you forget it.
recover.qr_help: The text under the QR code on page 1 of the emergency sheet. It may span several lines there: copy it whole, in one go. Spaces and line breaks are ignored. A device that remembers this account may leave it empty.
recover.qr_label: Text of the sheet's QR code (page 1)
recover.reset_open: A recovery session for this browser is still open (it lasts 30 minutes), so the code you already used is not needed again for the same e-mail address.
recover.rk_help: The key that starts with FFR1 on page 2 of your emergency sheet. A typing error is caught before anything is sent.
recover.secret_key_help: The secret key stays the same. Type it from page 1 of your emergency sheet.
recover.signed_in: You are signed in as {email}, so no one-time code is needed.
recover.title: Recover account
